content: Weston General Hospital is a National Health Service (NHS) district general hospital located in Weston-super-Mare, North Somerset, England. It is managed by the Weston Area Health NHS Trust (WAHT). The hospital is equipped with an Accident & Emergency department, an intensive care unit, an Oncology and Haematology day unit, and a day case unit. It has a total of 358 beds and employs approximately 1,800 staff members. Notably, it houses the largest midwifery-led maternity unit in the country. Additionally, the hospital operates a 12-bed private unit called The Waterside Suite, which is fully owned by the hospital trust, with all profits reinvested into the main hospital. The Healthcare Commission, an independent body that promotes and ensures quality healthcare in the United Kingdom, has inspected Weston General Hospital and published its findings. During the 2005/2006 period, the hospital's quality of healthcare was rated as weak on a four-point scale (weak, fair, good, excellent), placing it among the bottom 9% of trusts in the country. Its use of resources was also rated as weak, ranking it in the bottom 37% of trusts. In the 2006/2007 period, the hospital's quality of healthcare rating improved to fair, but its use of resources remained weak. Like many other hospitals, Weston General has faced challenges with hospital-acquired infections, including Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) and Clostridium difficile (C. diff). In 2003, the trust had the highest rate of MRSA infections in the country. In August 2007, the hospital faced criticism in the local press following the death of a 75-year-old cancer patient from C. diff. In response, the hospital reported a 25% reduction in infection rates during 2007, attributing the improvement to initiatives such as the bare below the elbow policy, which ensures staff clean their hands and wrists, and regular steam cleaning of patient beds. On July 7, 2003, the BBC television program Inside Out aired allegations from a whistleblower that senior management at the hospital had pressured employees to manipulate waiting list statistics to present more favorable data. An independent inquiry in 2004 confirmed that such manipulation had occurred. In 2006, one of the managers named in the Inside Out program lost a libel case against the BBC, which had alleged her involvement in falsifying waiting lists. Waiting lists remain a concern; in 2006, the hospital was one of only eight in the country that failed to reduce waiting times for treatment. The hospital has a rich history. Their Royal Highnesses, the Duke and Duchess of York (later King George VI and Queen Elizabeth, the Queen Mother), officially opened the Queen Alexandra Memorial Hospital on The Boulevard in 1928. Over the years, the hospital expanded with the addition of new equipment and temporary buildings to meet the growing needs of the community. With the town of Weston and the surrounding area, particularly Worle, experiencing significant growth, it became evident that a new hospital was needed. After much debate, a new hospital was constructed and opened on September 16, 1986, on the edge of Uphill village. In January 2003, the hospital opened a new Oncology and Haematology day unit, the Jackson Barstow Wing, to provide treatments such as chemotherapy and blood transfusions to patients from the surrounding area, eliminating the need to travel to Bristol. In February 2007, Weston General Hospital opened a new pediatric unit, the Seashore Centre, which includes pediatric outpatient services and a 10-bed day ward. This unit was established because the only major children's facilities in the region are located at Bristol Children's Hospital and Musgrove Park Hospital in Taunton. The hospital is supported by several voluntary organizations. The League of Friends, an active group of volunteers, staffs the hospital shop and raises funds for various projects within the hospital. Freewheelers Emergency Voluntary Service uses motorcycles to provide out-of-hours emergency transport for blood, diagnostic specimens, and medications. Sunshine Radio, a hospital radio station, is operated by volunteers. The hospital also collaborates closely with Weston Hospicecare, which provides palliative care for patients with life-threatening conditions such as cancer. The new children's center was partially funded by a community appeal called Weston Super Kids, which received widespread support from the town, including the Mayor, who made it her chosen charity during her term in office.
